english.title: Assault secure training centre custody officer

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: CRIMINAL JUSTICE AND PUBLIC ORDER ACT 1994

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) assaulted **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), a custody officer

(A)_[acting in pursuance of escort arrangements]_
(B)_[performing custodial duties at a contracted out secure training centre]_
(C)_[performing contracted out functions at a directly managed secure training centre]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 13(1) of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
assaulted a custody officer
acting as escort/performing custodial duties at contracted out training centre/performing contracted functions at directly managed secure training centre

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Custody officer must be readily identifiable as such when acting in pursuance of escort arrangements - see section 13(3) of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994.
(ii) See section 15 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994 for definitions.
(iii) Section 40(3) of the Criminal Justice Act 1988 was amended by the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994 (paragraph 35 schedule 9) to include an offence under this section. This allows the offence to be added to an indictment if necessary.
(iv) Section 17(2) of the Firearms Act 1968 (additional penalty for possession of firearms when committed certain offences) applies to this offence. See also associated offence wordings H2203, H2204 and H2206.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.
(See note (iii) concerning mode of trial).

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
